prescription = a written order from a doctor for a medicine
generic drug = a medicine with the same active ingredient as a brand-name product, usually cheaper
over-the-counter medicine = a drug you can buy without a doctor’s order
recommended dose = the amount of a medicine that should be taken at one time
side effect = an unwanted result of a medicine or treatment
clinical trial = a carefully controlled test of a new treatment in people
placebo = a dummy treatment with no active drug, used to test whether a medicine really works
surgery = a medical operation that involves cutting or repairing the body
keyhole surgery = an operation done through small cuts, often with a camera
organ transplant = an operation that replaces a failing organ with one from a donor
organ donor = a person who gives an organ for transplant, in life or after death
blood transfusion = putting donated blood into a patient’s vein
physiotherapy = treatment that uses movement, exercise and massage to restore function
occupational therapy = treatment that helps people manage daily tasks after illness or disability
alternative medicine = treatments outside standard scientific medicine, such as some herbal or needle therapies
acupuncture = a therapy that uses thin needles at specific points on the body
medical rehabilitation = a programme of therapy to regain strength or skills after illness or injury
palliative care = care that relieves pain and stress when a disease cannot be cured
hospice = a place or service that cares for people with a terminal illness
pain management = planned medical help to reduce long-term or severe pain
